title: CI never runs lore check, although a green lore check is the definition of done for a docs change
description:
Reported by opum-agent 2026-09-15 14:42Z (OPAG-146): measured by ref on origin/dev at 14:34Z, eight of ten fleet repos, this one included, have no CI job running `lore check`, while the shared operating block makes a green `lore check` the definition of done for any docs-touching change. Here the gate is enforced only by whoever remembers to run it by hand before opening a PR.

Why this repository cannot copy the fleet reference job verbatim: opum-agent and opum-doc install a published @opum-ai/quest alongside lore, because lore's quest adapter shells out to the `quest` binary on PATH (verified here: a shim that exits 1 makes `lore check` throw validation "`quest --version` did not report a supported Quest version", so the dependency is a subprocess contract, not a file read). This repository AUTHORS quest, so a published pin has the same two defects Tracker integrity already documents: it cannot see a regression the PR itself introduces, and it goes red on every version-bump PR because the declared version is not published yet. The job must therefore run lore against the quest built from the PR's own checkout, the way tracker-integrity.yml does. Verified locally 2026-09-15: with a `quest` shim on PATH that execs `bun run src/cli/main.ts`, `lore check` reports 63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A GitHub Actions job named `lore check` runs `lore check` on every pull request into dev, and on push to dev and main so the context can later become a required check without deadlocking the fast-forward promotion; green on this task's own PR run, cited by PR number and run id

lore's quest subprocess resolves to the quest built from the PR's own checkout, not a published version: the job log prints the shim path and the version it reports, and the workflow installs no @opum-ai/quest
An error-tier lore finding fails the job: the exit-6 path is proven by a deliberate negative test whose evidence is recorded in the task notes, not assumed from the docs
CHANGELOG.md Unreleased records the addition under Added, naming the workflow file

plan: 1. Add .github/workflows/lore-check.yml modelled on tracker-integrity.yml: pull_request + push on dev/main, pinned actions, bun 1.3.14, frozen lockfile install.
2. Put a `quest` shim on PATH that execs `bun run src/cli/main.ts` from the checkout; print the shim path and `quest --version` in the log.
3. Install @opum-ai/lore pinned at the version paired with this package (0.7.0 today) and run `lore check`.
4. Negative-test the exit-6 path locally against the same shim, record the evidence in a note.
5. CHANGELOG Unreleased/Added entry; lore check green locally; PR into dev; cite PR number and run id; close in the same PR.
implementationNotes:
NEGATIVE TEST OF THE EXIT-6 PATH, run locally 2026-09-15 against the same shim shape the workflow installs (a `quest` on PATH that execs `bun run src/cli/main.ts` from this checkout, lore 0.7.0). Appended a link to a file that does not exist to docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, ran `lore check --json`: errorCount 1, finding rule broken-link severity error on runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, exit 6. Restored the file byte-for-byte from a copy taken before the edit (git status clean under docs/), re-ran: 63 files, errorCount 0, warningCount 0, exit 0. So an error-tier finding reds the job through the plain exit code, no --strict needed.

SECOND NEGATIVE TEST, the subprocess contract: a `quest` shim that prints its arguments and exits 1 makes `lore check --json` emit a report with complete:false followed by a validation error envelope ("`quest --version` did not report a supported Quest version", hint "Quest 0.2.7 or newer is required"). That is what proves lore resolves quest via PATH at run time rather than via any cached or bundled path, and it is why the workflow asserts what `command -v quest` resolves to before running lore.

TOOLING: actionlint (installed locally) exits 0 on the new workflow. The workflow pins lore at 0.7.0 explicitly rather than deriving it from package.json, because on a version-bump PR the paired lore is not published yet and a derived pin would red exactly the PR that cuts a release; the comment in the file says so.
